guide_enrichment.narrative:
We understand why Missouri’s stock is high after a 54-14 opening win. Austin Simmons completed 17 of 19 passes for 252 yards and four touchdowns without an interception, while the defense allowed only 198 total yards. We are not dismissing that performance, but we also are not treating one dominant result as proof that Missouri should command this much separation.

The more interesting part for us is Missouri’s defensive turnover. Missouri returned only two defensive starters and lost 10, including its two leading sack producers from 2025. Experienced transfers help address that turnover, but our view is that the market is pricing more certainty into this defense than one game can establish. Our case is not that Troy owns the better matchup; it is that the available cushion accounts for Troy’s limitations and then some.

The concern is clear in our efficiency numbers. Troy has struggled to generate value through both the air and on the ground, and its scoring-opportunity rate has been a particular weakness. Missouri’s defense grades well in the areas most likely to keep Troy pinned back. That gives Missouri a credible path to separation, but we still think the market has stretched beyond our longer-run expectation.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Troy’s passing offense against Missouri’s pass defense. Missouri forced Arkansas-Pine Bluff into a 3-of-13 third-down performance and five three-and-outs in the opener, while our numbers rate Troy’s passing efficiency as a major disadvantage in this matchup. Troy does not need to control the game offensively for our position to work, but it does need enough completions and sustained drives to prevent Missouri from repeatedly starting with favorable field position.

recent_game.fact: Missouri opened the 2026 season with a 54-14 home win over Arkansas-Pine Bluff on September 3.
Missouri produced 562 total yards against Arkansas-Pine Bluff, with 357 passing yards and 205 rushing yards.
Missouri led Arkansas-Pine Bluff 40-0 at halftime and held a 376-6 advantage in first-half yardage.
Missouri converted 6 of 10 third downs, both fourth-down attempts and all five red-zone opportunities against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.
Missouri's defense allowed 198 total yards, 13 first downs and a 3-of-13 third-down conversion rate in the opener.

opponent_notes.fact: Missouri is scheduled to host Troy on September 19, 2026, at 6 p.m. CT on SECN+.

quarterback.fact: Ole Miss transfer Austin Simmons is listed as Missouri's starting quarterback, with sophomore Matt Zollers as the backup.
In his Missouri debut, Simmons completed 17 of 19 passes for 252 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.
Simmons' 89.5% completion rate and 270.4 passer rating were the highest by a quarterback in his Missouri debut.
Simmons is the seventh different starting quarterback of Eli Drinkwitz's Missouri tenure and the third transfer quarterback to start in that span.
Zollers appeared in the opener and completed 8 of 12 passes for 87 yards while scoring his first collegiate rushing touchdown.

offensive_personnel.fact: Missouri lists Cayden Green at left tackle, Tristan Wilson at left guard, Dominick Giudice at center, Curtis Peagler at right guard and Luke Work at right tackle on its current depth chart.
Missouri returned five offensive starters from 2025: Cayden Green, Dominick Giudice, Ahmad Hardy, Brett Norfleet and Curtis Peagler.
Missouri lost six offensive starters from 2025, including quarterback Beau Pribula, center Connor Tollison, tackle Keagan Trost and three wide receivers.
Ole Miss transfer Cayden Lee is listed as a starting receiver after starting all 15 games for Ole Miss in 2025 and 12 of 13 games in 2024.
Simmons connected with Lee five times for 89 yards in the opener, including a 47-yard touchdown.
Sophomore receiver Donovan Olugbode recorded seven receptions, 107 yards and two touchdowns in the opener according to Missouri's game-note narrative.
Running back Jamal Roberts is listed atop the current depth chart and carried 13 times for 47 yards and one touchdown in the opener.
Roberts surpassed 1,000 career rushing yards during the season-opening win.
Tight ends Brett Norfleet and Jordon Harris are listed as co-starters on the current depth chart.

defensive_personnel.fact: Missouri returned only two defensive starters from 2025 and lost 10, including both leading 2025 sack producers Zion Young and Damon Wilson II.
Linebacker Nicholas Rodriguez and safety Santana Banner ranked second and third on Missouri in tackles in 2025 and entered 2026 with three and one prior Missouri starts, respectively.
Missouri added experienced SEC starters Robert Woodyard Jr. at linebacker and Chris Graves Jr. at cornerback through the transfer portal.
Woodyard started 11 games for Auburn in 2025 and recorded 67 tackles, including 50 in conference play.
Graves appeared in 41 games over three seasons at Ole Miss and started nine games in 2025.
Defensive tackles Marquis Gracial and Sterling Webb combined for six tackles for loss in 2025; Webb also had 2.5 sacks and six quarterback hurries.
Darris Smith, listed as Missouri's starting JACK, recorded four sacks as a pass-rush specialist in 2025.

coaching_changes.fact: Chip Lindsey joined Missouri as offensive coordinator in December 2025 after previous coordinator jobs at Michigan, North Carolina, Auburn, Arizona State, UCF and Southern Miss.
Lindsey was Troy's head coach from 2019 through 2021.
Garrett Riley joined Missouri in January 2026 as quarterbacks coach after serving as Clemson's offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach.
John Papuchis became Missouri's special-teams coordinator and defensive assistant in January 2026 after six seasons coordinating Florida State's special teams.
Derek Nicholson added co-defensive coordinator to his linebackers-coach title before the 2026 season.

offensive_context.fact: Missouri averaged 228.3 rushing yards per game in 2025, eighth nationally and first in the SEC.
Missouri had a program-record 12 individual 100-yard rushing performances in 2025.
Missouri rushed for 31 touchdowns in 2025 and scored three rushing touchdowns in its 2026 opener.
In the opener, Missouri averaged 7.2 yards per play, converted 60% of its third downs and scored touchdowns on four of five red-zone possessions.

defensive_context.fact: Missouri's 2025 defense allowed 277.3 yards and 18.9 points per game, including 103.8 rushing yards and 173.5 passing yards per game.
The 2025 defense allowed 4.5 yards per play and opponents converted 35% of their third downs.
Missouri forced five three-and-outs against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.
Missouri did not record a takeaway in its season opener.

special_teams.fact: Blake Craig is listed as Missouri's starting placekicker and made a 32-yard field goal plus all seven extra-point attempts in the opener.
Brunno Reus is listed as Missouri's starting punter, kickoff specialist and holder.
DaMarion Fowlkes is listed as the primary punt and kickoff returner and had a 23-yard punt return in the opener.

other_relevant.fact: Missouri has won 24 consecutive home games against non-SEC opponents, a streak dating to October 21, 2017.
Missouri has won 12 consecutive home night games and 14 consecutive regular-season night games overall.

Missouri Athletics plans to recognize the undefeated 1960 team during halftime of the September 19 game against Troy, and Missouri will wear throwback uniforms for the Memorial Stadium 100th Anniversary Game.
